# Parity fixture — where `expected-findings.json` came from

`expected-findings.json` is **not** output of the code in this repo. It was
generated by the implementation `aggregate/normalize.py` was ported from, so that
the port has something to be wrong against:

```
PYTHONUTF8=1 python3 <Own.NET>/audit/aggregate/normalize.py \
  --sarif own-check=own-check.sarif \
  --sarif codeql=codeql.sarif \
  --sarif infersharp=infersharp.sarif \
  --sarif roslyn=roslyn.sarif \
  --taxonomy <Own.NET>/audit/static/taxonomy/categories.yml \
  --strip /work --strip /work/target --strip target \
  --json expected-findings.json
```

Reference revision: `Own.NET@0ded835` (`audit/aggregate/normalize.py`, 367 lines,
reading `audit/static/taxonomy/categories.yml`, itself reading SARIF through
`scripts/oracle_compare.parse_sarif`).

`aggregate/tests/test_normalize.py` re-runs that command when `OWNNET_REF` points
at an Own.NET checkout and diffs the result against the committed bytes. Without
`OWNNET_REF` the test still compares the port's output to these bytes — it just
cannot re-attest where they came from, and says so.

## One deliberate divergence from the reference (#57)

The committed golden carries two `coverage` keys the reference implementation
does not emit:

```jsonc
"no_physical_location": 1,
"no_physical_location_by": { "own-check": { "OWN001": 1 } }
```

They were **added on purpose**, not regenerated. `own-check.sarif` carries 20
results and 19 have a usable physical location; the reference dropped the 20th
and counted it nowhere, which is precisely the defect #57 fixes — so the
reference cannot produce these keys by construction, and waiting for it to would
mean never fixing the hole.

The change to the payload here is the **goal** of that slice, not a side effect
of it. Everything else in this file is untouched: `findings` is byte-identical to
what the reference produced, and the edit that added the two keys was an
additions-only diff. `_reference_checks` lifts exactly these two keys out (they
are listed in `DIVERGES_FROM_REFERENCE`), asserts their shape separately, and
holds the remaining bytes to the same equality it always did — so a real drift
cannot hide behind an intended divergence, and the intended divergence cannot
quietly grow.

## What the four SARIF inputs are for

They are hand-built, not captured, so every branch that matters is exercised at
least once and the diff stays readable (37 results, 34 scored):

| file | covers |
|---|---|
| `own-check.sarif` | the `OWN001` `[resource: ...]` umbrella split (subscription / timer / disposable field / pooled buffer / untagged `*` fallback, plus a case-and-space variant), `OWN014` region-escape, the `OWN050` coverage note, `XAML203`, an unmapped `XAML999` that the `XAML1*` net must **not** catch, every path spelling the tools emit (backslashes, `file:///`, `./`, overlapping strip prefixes), and the degenerate result shapes: no `startLine`, non-integer `startLine`, no location at all, `rule.id` instead of `ruleId`, no message, empty `ruleId` |
| `codeql.sarif` | cross-tool agreement at a site own-check also flags, third-party suppression by **path** and by **message**, an unmapped rule |
| `infersharp.sarif` | the `*RESOURCE_LEAK` / `*MEMORY_LEAK` globs, and Infer# rules with no taxonomy entry |
| `roslyn.sarif` | glob precedence (`CA2000` exact beats `CA2*`; `CA1*`, `IDISP0*`, `INPC0*`, `WPF0*`), and a compiler diagnostic with no entry |

The `--strip` list deliberately contains three overlapping spellings of one
worktree — that is what `Run-Audit.ps1` passes, and it is what makes
longest-prefix stripping observable instead of theoretical.

## Beyond the fixture

The port was also run against the recorded STS corpus in `sts_audit/`
(`ownsharp.sarif` + `codeql.sarif` + `infersharp.sarif` + `roslyn.sarif`,
73 397 results, 72 559 scored, 25.8 MB of JSON) side by side with the reference
implementation: the two payloads are byte-identical. That run is not committed —
the inputs are 100 MB — but it is reproducible from this repo with the command in
`docs/normalization.md`.
